title: A new level: real objects
say: You have learned to see the cube, sphere, cone, and cylinder. Now let's use that knowledge with a real object. Now we will study an apple. It grows from the sphere you know, but it leans, dips around the stem, and has its own uneven shape. Let's look before we draw.
hint: A sphere becomes a real apple

captions.text: You have learned to see the cube sphere cone
and cylinder Now let's use that knowledge with a
real object Now we will study an apple It
grows from the sphere you know but it leans
dips around the stem and has its own uneven
shape Let's look before we draw

title: Turn it and look again
say: Turn this apple with your finger or the arrows. Watch the top dip and the uneven shoulders move around the form. A real apple doesn't stay perfectly round from every view. Find a view you like, then bring that careful looking into your drawing.
hint: Turn · Notice the dip · Compare both sides

captions.text: Turn this apple with your finger or the arrows
Watch the top dip and the uneven shoulders move
around the form A real apple doesn't stay perfectly
round from every view Find a view you like
then bring that careful looking into your drawing

title: Find the form under the skin
say: Here is your teacher's finished drawing. Tap the three spots to find the stem dip, the turning surface, and the shadow that anchors it to the table. You already know the sphere's light and dark. Now notice how those ideas follow an apple's less perfect surface.
hint: Tap the three clues in the drawing

title: Keep the familiar tools close
say: Bring your sketch paper, pencils, and eraser. Start with a light pencil for construction. We will switch pencils when the value grows darker, and keep the light areas clean. Choose the textured side of your paper if you want the graphite to grip it.

title: More than a sphere
chapter: Build an apple from the sphere

title: Hatching follows the terminator
say: Follow the turning edge with your pencil strokes. Their direction helps describe the apple's rounded skin. Take your time with this on your page. Press continue when you are ready.

title: Darken with 2B

title: Strokes that build texture

title: Observe, don't chase the outline
say: Unlike basic forms, the apple has specific texture and direction. Observe the stem groove, dimples, body undulations — feel it. Take your time with this on your page. Press continue when you are ready.

title: Soften the terminator

title: Top plane lifts as one
say: The top is not flat. Watch the direction of the pencil as it follows the surface rising toward the stem. Take your time with this on your page. Press continue when you are ready.

title: Look again at an everyday apple
say: Next time you see an apple, turn it in your hand. Where does it resemble a sphere? Where does it become its own shape? That observation is a skill you can take into every still life.
hint: The sphere was only the beginning
